newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Sberbank sees lower profit in 97 - chairman.
newsitem.headline: Russia Sberbank sees lower profit in 97 - chairman.

text.p: Russia's biggest bank, Sberegatelny Bank RF (Sberbank), will have a lower profit in 1997 due to falling interest rates, its chairman said on Monday.
"We cannot count on increasing (profit) volumes," Andrei Kazmin told a news conference. "A fall in the price of resources will lead to a fall in profit in all banks."
Sberbank's 1996 pre-tax profit soared to 14.5 trillion roubles ($2.5 billion) from 4.3 trillion roubles in 1995.
The Central Bank cut its main interest rate to 36 percent from 42 percent from Monday.
The news, announced on April 24, immediately pushed down yields on the government securities market -- the main source of profit-making for many Russian banks.
Kazmin said in 1996 Sberbank carried out a major restructuring programme to unify the process of managing liquidity, risks, credit and rates.
"The amount of work and the character of goals is totally new for us," Kazmin said. "We have achieved a very serious progress in all key issues."
For the first time in its history Sberbank is undergoing an audit to international standards by Price Waterhouse, he said.
One of the aims of the audit is to help attract foreign capital by placing debt papers on the international market, he said.
He gave no details, but said he did not rule out a Eurobond issue.
On the domestic bank share market, Sberbank is the most liquid and highly capitalised stock.
Kazmin said the bank planned several small share issues in the future.
"There will be several share issues, by they will be small by volume, as the market is narrow," he said.
He said the Central Bank was now registering a new share issue, but said the volume would not exceed 50 billion roubles.
Sberbank is quoted on the RTS-2 second-tier market for less liquid stocks. On Friday it closed at $120.05.
